headline: Chinese AI Models Are 10x Cheaper Than GPT-4o, Dev Finds
summary: A developer discovered AI models priced as low as $0.01 per million tokens, challenging the perception of AI as an expensive technology.
details: A recent discovery by a developer has revealed that many Chinese AI models are significantly cheaper than popular Western alternatives. Models are available for as little as $0.01 per million tokens, challenging the common assumption that advanced AI comes with a high price tag.

The developer, initially hesitant about AI costs after a brief experience with OpenAI's API, found Global API listing 184 different models. This opened their eyes to a vast ecosystem of affordable AI solutions previously overlooked.

Comparing prices, GPT-4o costs $2.50 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens. In contrast, models like DeepSeek V4 Flash are priced at $0.27 input and $1.10 output, with similar or better benchmark performance.
Other competitive options include Qwen3-32B at $0.30/$1.20 and GLM-4 Plus at $0.20/$0.80 per million tokens, all representing a fraction of GPT-4o's cost.

The developer's initial project, a customer support ticket summarizer, was nearly abandoned due to the perceived cost of using GPT-4o, which consumed $4 in a single session. This led to the realization that AI might be inaccessible for those without substantial budgets.
Upon switching to a cheaper Chinese model via Global API, the same summarization task cost only $0.02, proving the viability of affordable AI for practical applications and portfolio projects.

Remarkably, Global API supports the OpenAI SDK, allowing developers to switch models by simply changing the base URL and model name. This ease of integration means minimal learning curve for those already familiar with the OpenAI library.

This accessibility contrasts sharply with complex setups like self-hosted LLaMA, which can take days to configure. The developer achieved a working API in minutes, highlighting the user-friendliness of these platforms.

The developer further built a more robust version of the ticket summarizer, incorporating streaming and error handling, demonstrating how easily practical AI tools can be developed with these cost-effective models.
